title.narrative: Transition for inclusive development in Eastern DRC (TRIDE)

description.narrative: **General objective: ** Alleviation of insecurity and instability by promoting economic development and access to markets and land in Eastern DRC. **Key-objectives:** • Outcome 1: Access to land by smallholders is increased, security of tenure for smallholders is improved and land-related conflicts are reduced; • Outcome 2: Integrated Water Resources Management is strengthened to promote resilient agricultural systems in North and South Kivu; • Outcome 3: The local economy is revitalized through inclusive and profitable value chains and the development of market systems.
• (Vulnerable) smallholder farmers and their families in rural villages,• Market actors,• (Local) Public authorities.

comment.narrative: 11 co-ops out of the 45 targeted by the project, 21 of which will be supervised in 2022) (24.4%).A cooperative will be considered well managed and functional when it has at least five of the following elements of enterprise management: up-to-date accounts; management tools; a management committee and/or board of directors; organises at least quarterly management meetings and once a year a general assembly of members; has its own resources to ensure its activities (financial and operational autonomy); has a bank account for savings and investments with at least two signatories.The co-operatives that meet at least 5 of these criteria and are judged to be well managed are the following 11: SOPACDI Kalehe CaféAMKA Kalehe CaféCOAPAKA Masisi PotatoesCOOPAKIRU Rutshuru MaizeLA PEPINIERE Rutshuru Savings & creditCOOAPATU Masisi PotatoesCOOCAPA Uvira RiceCOOPRITU Uvira RiceCOOPABA Uvira RiceUCADI Uvira RiceCOOPEC-RUZIZI Uvira Savings & creditOf the 21 cooperatives accompanied in 2022, 9 (42.9%) have up-to-date accounts, and 18 (85.7%) have management tools. All cooperatives (100%) have boards of directors in place, and among them, 15 (71.4%) hold at least one meeting per quarter and (10) 47.6% have organised their ordinary general assemblies in 2022. 17 (81%) of the 21 cooperatives have two signatories to the bank accounts. In sum, 11 of the 21 cooperatives (52.4%) meet at least 5 of the 7 criteria for the year 2022.

13 cooperatives out of the 45 are well-managed, with an inclusive and functioning governance structure. No new cooperatives have been added this quarter, as the project continued with the same 13 cooperatives as in 2023.

17 cooperatives out of the 45 have been supported, demonstrating 37,77% of the cooperatives are well managed with an inclusive and functioning governance structure. In Q3, 37,77%, or 17/45 cooperatives improved their governance.

18 of the 45 cooperatives, or 40%, meet at least 5 of the 7 criteria for the proper functioning of cooperatives as defined by the project. Compared to the results of Q4/2024, one cooperative improved its score, notably with the completion of its first audit of its accounts.
No new cooperative for this quarter, as we have continued with the same ones as in 2023
SOPACDI, AMKA, COAPAKA, COOPAKIRU, LA PEPINIERE, COOAPATU, COOCAPA, COOPRITU, COOPABA, UCADI, COOPEC-RUZIZI, CAM and SOPACDI. Note that some are now in the inaccessible area in Masisi and Rutsuru.

The results on the governance of cooperatives remained the same. 17 of the 45 cooperatives targeted by the project (37.77%) meet at least 5 of the 7 criteria for the proper functioning of cooperatives as defined by the project. More specifically, of the 42 cooperatives supported, 33% have up-to-date accounts, 52% have management tools. All cooperatives (100%) have boards of directors in place and among them 60% hold at least one meeting per quarter and 38% have organized their ordinary general meetings in 2024. 48% of 42 cooperatives have two signatories to the accounts

title.narrative: Outcome 3 - Local economy is revitalized through inclusive development and profitable value chains and the market system (MSD)
# of jobs created

description.narrative: Jobs created refers to the number of formal jobs (employees with an employment contract) and informal (without contract) created within TRIDE c's target value chains and at farm level.This indicator refers only to Staff employment creation, it does not only focus on creation of employment of cooperative staff but also of value chain contracted actors’ staff. The frequency is on an annual basis. The target value of this indicator is the sum of the targets for each year of the life of the project.

comment.narrative: 106 jobs were created between April and June 2024, of which 79 are casual jobs, and 27 are permanent jobs. Out of the 106 jobs, 37 jobs are for women and 92 are for youth.
168 casual jobs were created between January and March 2024, of which 34 are jobs for women and 66 for youth
330 jobs have been created during Q4, of which 14 permanent and 316 casual jobs
85 jobs were created between July and September 2024, of which 76 are casual jobs and 9 are permanent jobs.
89 jobs have been created, of which 21 permanent jobs and 68 casual jobs have been created. 20 are jobs for women.

In South Kivu, 106 jobs were created, including 36 for young people under 35 and 12 for women. In North Kivu, by the end of 2022, the TRIDE project has created 60 jobs, of which 55 are for young people and 7 for women
No new jobs were created during the period. With the volatility of the security situation in the intervention zone, the volume of the activites was low with influence to the creation of new jobs.

title.narrative: Output 3.6 Home-based or larger-scale processing facilities and innovative post-harvest activities are introduced and enhanced
Number of agricultural product processing enterprises from value chains supported by the project put in touch with cooperatives and/or sales market

description.narrative: This indicator is about agricultural product processing facilities from value chains actors supported by the project that are linked with cooperatives but also about the support of new processing units of the value chain actors linked to the coopperatives.Viable processing facilities are those with the necessary equipment for their operation and maintenance, adapted to the main agricultural or livestock products of the entities. They will be considered in contact with cooperatives or markets when there is a sales contract between the two parties The target value of this indicator is the sum of the targets for each year of the life of the project.

comment.narrative: Five enterpreneurial and innovative processing units have been supported. Five entrepreneurial ideas have been supported. The innovative ideas concern several value chains, including rice, dairy, and coffee. The idea in coffee is about using coffee waste to produce soap. Two main ideas were supported in rice: fortification of rice combined with maize and steaming rice. Two ideas related to dairy are about milk processing : cheese and yougourt
No new enterprise supported. Focus was on providing support and coaching to already supported enterprises
No new enterprises have been established in Q1 of 2024, as we have continued supporting the same ones as in 2023
One local coffee SME (Short and Medium Enterprise) has been successfully put in touch with one supported cooperative after participating in awareness campaign about local consumption
There is no new agricultural product processing enterprises from value chains supported during this quarter, as the project continued to support the already established enterprises from 2023
We targeting 8 at the end of 2023. The identification process is ongoing; support to be done during Q4

title.narrative: Output 3.2 Value chain actors improved their capacities and have better access to finance through formal institutions
Volume of credits obtained by the cooperatives accompanied in the value chains

description.narrative: The volume of credit obtained by the cooperatives accompanied in the value chains represents the total amount of credit received by the cooperatives within a defined period of time

comment.narrative: COOPAMAK received a loan of USD 45000 from Equity-Bcdc during the quarter. In addition, COAPAKA received 33000 of loans from UMOJA SACCO in Goma.

COOPAMAK, a rice cooperative, secured credit for rice collection from a local bank. The project was not able to reach the 409,000 planned for Q4_2024, and the cumulative planned of 1,022,000 for year 2024.
From April to june 2024, $98000 of loans were provided to two cooperatives: $70,000 for AMKA (coffee) and $28,000 for CAT KIVU (Coffee)
From January to March 2024, $435000 in credit was received by four cooperatives: $108,000 by KCCO (coffee) and $33,000 by COOPAMAK (rice), $139000 by SCPNCK (Coffee), $155000 by AMKA
From July to September 2024, $80 000 of loans were provided to one cooperative, COOPAMAK (Rice)

The SCPCNK agricultural cooperative, which specialises in the production and sales of specialty coffee, mobilised USD 120,000 in loans. The loan was granted by SMICO ($70,000) and PAIDEK ($50,000). The mission of the round table of financial institutions with cooperative managers, organized by AGRITERRA in December 2024, accelerated the credit-granting processes that were still pending.

Three cooperatives have accessed 1,100 million USD. These are AMKA (Coffee value chain) for 672 thousand USD, COOPAMAK (Rice value chain) for 30 thousand USD and SOPACDI (Coffee value chain) for 310 thousand USD
Until the end of Q1 2023, a total of US$172000,000 in credit has been obtained by the cooperatives supported by the TRIDE project
